body: 225088 Gonggong and its separate satellite Xiangliu
status: research-only; no 85th dossier or production input change

paper.title: The mass and density of the dwarf planet (225088) 2007 OR10
paper.rights: Specific arXiv record uses nonexclusive distribution, not CC BY. ESA/Hubble image CC BY 4.0 does not license this paper or its figures. No figure embedded. Final publisher version/publication chronology not audited.

inspection.text: Complete 12-page extraction retained; targeted sections 7–8 and Figure 3 caption.
inspection.visual: Complete rendered pages 8, 9 and 10 inspected, including Figure 3 axes, caption and conclusions. Page 7 beginning of section 7 inspected in preceding orbit/thermal audit.
inspection.reproduction: No Monte Carlo, tidal integration, TinyTim reduction or physical-axis inference reproduced.

monteCarloAssumptions.constrainedInputs: Authors sample orbit parameters and system mass as normal distributions using fitted values/uncertainties. Primary H_V=2.34±0.01 and satellite H_V=6.93±0.15 also sampled normally; primary thermal section used ±0.05 separately.
monteCarloAssumptions.limits: Satellite radius is derived from assumed albedo and absolute magnitude. Q and formation age are priors, not direct measurements or proof of origin.

conditionalResults.circularization: Requiring circularization time longer than assumed 4.5 Gyr gives q<4e-4, satellite effective radius 18–50 km, geometric albedo 1.0–0.2 and Q>100 in the authors’ sampled configurations. Not a direct radius/albedo/mass measurement; do not replace historical publisher 240–400 km diameter silently.
conditionalResults.despinning: Authors obtain satellite despinning time below 1e7 yr for all sampled configurations and infer likely locking. Primary time falls below 4.5 Gyr only for q>2e-2, which conflicts with retaining eccentricity under their circularization assumptions; permitted configurations give primary times above 1e12 yr. Model-inferred locking is not measured satellite rotation/pole or registered permanent-face geography.
conditionalResults.angularMomentum: Combined spin/orbit normalized angular momentum tends to ~0.4 at small q and remains below 0.8; compatibility with a single-collision criterion is not an observed collision or unique history.
conditionalResults.kozai: Quadrupole solar-perturbation models permit prograde e0–.65/i39–54 degrees or retrograde e0–.63/i127–141, nominal ~2e6 yr timescale. Conditional initially circular evolution at ~54 degrees and nonzero present eccentricity gives q<=5e-3. These are distinct model constraints, not a measured uncertainty interval or a present ephemeris.
conditionalResults.oblateness: Homogeneous-density Maclaurin assumptions give flattening .0026–.0118, J2 .0001–.04 and a/ac .35–.49, suggesting present oblateness-dominated dynamics. Reported precession times are 5.4e4–4.2e5 yr prograde and 1.8e4–1.4e5 yr retrograde. Not measured axes, J2, internal composition, spin pole or image registration. Authors flag the remaining noncircular-orbit problem.

psfAlternative.hypothesis: A nearby tidally locked double primary was considered as an alternative explanation of the light curve.
psfAlternative.publisherNumbers: Authors quote hypothetical separation 4250 km / 67 mas, TinyTim relative brightness trials 1:2–1:20, and no notable 2017 PSF distortion down to their claimed 1:10 detectability. These are quoted author values, not new angular/raster computations.
psfAlternative.limits: No new companion discovered; non-detection is limited to tested PSFs, epochs, separations and brightness, not exhaustive absence. No raw image/PSF pipeline reprocessing or transfer to the ESA collage.

conclusions.unresolvedHistory: Authors explicitly do not identify a unique mechanism producing the orbit. Distant capture followed by Kozai pumping/tidal shrinkage, and spin-orbit resonance alternatives, remain scenarios rather than observed history.
conclusions.spinAndSize: Small bright satellite preference under these assumptions does not independently settle primary 22.4/44.8h alternatives, unique thermal size/density, or equator-orbit alignment. Conclusions use ~45h language; preserve alongside preferred 22.4h thermal cases.
conclusions.noAnalogs: Comparisons to Pluto/Charon/Quaoar/Haumea and their moons are dynamical context, never permission to reuse their surface maps.
